podcast.body: Released in March 1994, this single catapulted Blur to immense success both within and outside the United Kingdom, becoming an anthem across Europe. Its release shortly before the "Parklife" album was instrumental in establishing Blur as a leading force in Britpop.

This song is listed as containing the "devil's tri tone" (flattened fifth). This reference showcases the widespread application of this dissonant interval across different subgenres of rock and pop music, indicating its versatility. "In addition to a ton of Sabbath and Hendrix songs, they can also be heard in David Bowie's station to station, the beautiful people by Marilyn Manson, Blurred Girls and Boys, SIGDIS X1 and YYZ by Rush, Enter Sandman from Metallica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
